**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

Section 15.2 ("Assignment; Change of Control") satisfies the preferred position on all material terms from our side:

- **Our assignment rights**: We may assign to any Sanofi Affiliate without RevMed's consent, and may assign the Agreement in whole, without consent, to a successor in a sale of all or substantially all relevant assets or in a merger/acquisition or similar transaction — the affiliate and M&A carve-outs the playbook requires.
- **Restriction on RevMed**: Asymmetric in our favour — RevMed's Affiliate assignments need our consent (not unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned), and transfers of RevMed Licensed Patents to Third Parties need our consent (15.2(b)). Acquiror-side assignments are further fenced by the Acquiror Family / Acquired Party Family firewall conditions (A)–(D).
- **No vendor exit on our change of control**: The only change-of-control termination right (Section 12.2(a)(ii)) runs in our favour, on a Change of Control of *RevMed*. RevMed's termination rights (material breach, insolvency, Competing Product, cessation of development) are not CoC-triggered.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged: (i) RevMed's successor assignment on its own Change of Control is not consent-gated and there is no express bar on assigning to a Sanofi competitor — mitigated by our 12.2(a)(ii) termination option; and (ii) Section 12.3 (p0508) cuts off RevMed's post-termination royalties to us on a Change of Control of Sanofi, which is back-end termination economics rather than a vendor exit/re-pricing right, and belongs under the termination-effects rule rather than being double-flagged here.
